title: `rank`: `average` by default; NULL ranks are NULL
description: `rank()` gives tied rows their average rank as a double; the methods `min`, `max`, `dense` and `ordinal` give integers. A NULL's rank is NULL (SQL ranks NULLs with the other rows), and `descending=True` reverses the order with NaN first. There is no `ntile`, `percent_rank` or `cume_dist` expression.
reference: `rank`, `dense_rank`, `row_number` over the window's order, NULLs placed by the key's direction; `percent_rank`, `cume_dist`, `ntile` as SQL.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.

evidence.note: 'ordinal': every value gets a distinct rank, in the order the values occur in the Series; 'random': ties ranked independently of that order (seeded by `seed`); Notes: only non-null values are ranked and nulls are kept
the window functions listed are `over` and `rolling`
the API index has no `ntile`, `percent_rank` or `cume_dist`

notes: `rank('ordinal')`, Polars's `ROW_NUMBER`, breaks ties by input order, so `over` with a pre-sorted frame keeps a stable sort's order of ties. `rank('min')` and `rank('dense')` give tied rows one rank. There is no NTILE, so `ntile_spread` and its tie order have no Polars counterpart: a plan with `ntile` is refused.
The docs at `stable` are those of Polars 2.1.0: their [source] links point at tag py-2.1.0.
